items.title: Joe Segal — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History
items.q: I had the privilege of seeing Dave Brubeck at Blues Alley

ctx.x: This way at least with four nights we’ve got a chance.

Yeah. I had the privilege of seeing Dave Brubeck at Blues Alley, it’s one of those rare moments - this is two, three years before he passed - that he actually agreed to play in a club, and I always thought as a musician... I mean I understand the appeal for a concert hall, but there’s nothing like playing in a club. Cause you have that immediacy within your audience. You have the opportunity, like you said, to play for multiple nights, and so you’re starting to develop a chemistry and a repertoire, more so with…

During the week, yeah. During the week we charge a lot less and of course we have to pay a lot less. But we pay them a nice wage, you know, and they come in. And there’s a lot of great local people. And actually we’re going to start featuring them more on the weekends too, come next year, so we don’t have to fight these hotel prices which are ridiculous.
